question: Which electrolyte did the KestrelCell use, and which company supplied it?
reference_answer: VX-9, a fluorinated ether electrolyte, supplied by Varn Materials.

evidence.quote: All cells used VX-9, a fluorinated ether electrolyte containing sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, supplied by Varn Materials

question: How many cycles did the median KestrelCell complete before reaching end of life?

evidence.quote: The median KestrelCell reached end of life after 2,400 cycles at 1C

question: What average water content did Varn Materials measure across the VX-9 batches released in 2024?
reference_answer: 12 parts per million on average (specification at most 20 ppm; highest batch 18 ppm).

evidence.quote: the average water content across the 186 batches released in 2024 was 12 parts per million

question: At what temperature does the Oskarsund Battery Test Centre run its accelerated ageing protocol?

evidence.quote: cells are cycled or stored at 45 degrees Celsius

question: What round-trip efficiency did the Norrby storage pilot achieve?
reference_answer: 87 percent over the whole pilot, including inverter and cooling-fan losses. (Not Norrvik's 91 percent, which is a different, LFP pilot.)

evidence.quote: round-trip efficiency at the grid connection was 87 percent

question: At which plant is the electrolyte used in the KestrelCell produced?
reference_answer: KestrelCell uses VX-9, which Varn Materials produces only at its Brekke plant.

evidence.quote: All cells used VX-9
VX-9 is produced only at our Brekke plant

question: Which electrolyte is used in the cell chemistry installed in the Norrby pilot?
reference_answer: The Norrby pilot used the chemistry of Kade and colleagues at the Halvik Institute, i.e. the KestrelCell, which uses Varn Materials' VX-9 electrolyte.

evidence.quote: used the room-temperature sodium-sulfur chemistry developed by Kade and colleagues at the Halvik Institute of Electrochemistry
All cells used VX-9

question: What average water content was measured in 2024 in the electrolyte of the chemistry used in the Norrby pilot?
reference_answer: Norrby used the Kade/Halvik chemistry (KestrelCell), whose electrolyte is VX-9; Varn measured an average of 12 ppm water in 2024 VX-9 batches.

evidence.quote: developed by Kade and colleagues at the Halvik Institute of Electrochemistry
All cells used VX-9
the average water content across the 186 batches released in 2024 was 12 parts per million

question: Who directs the laboratory where the cells behind the Norrby pilot's chemistry were cycle-tested?
reference_answer: The KestrelCell (the Kade/Halvik chemistry used at Norrby) was cycle-tested at the Oskarsund Battery Test Centre, directed by Dr. Amara Lindqvist.

evidence.quote: developed by Kade and colleagues at the Halvik Institute of Electrochemistry
Long-term cycling was carried out at the Oskarsund Battery Test Centre
Centre director: Dr. Amara Lindqvist

question: A Norrby module overheated when the outdoor temperature reached 43 degrees Celsius. Above what temperature did the paper describing that chemistry report accelerated capacity fade?
reference_answer: Above 40 degrees Celsius (at 45 degrees cells lasted roughly 900 cycles).

evidence.quote: the outdoor temperature at the substation reached 43 degrees Celsius
capacity fade accelerated sharply above 40 degrees Celsius

question: Was the electrolyte used in the KestrelCell affected by Varn Materials' 2024 recall?
reference_answer: No. The recall covered eleven batches of VX-7 (chloride contamination at the Solberg plant); KestrelCell uses VX-9, which the report says was not affected.

evidence.quote: All cells used VX-9
VX-9 and VX-11 were not affected by the recall

question: How did the Norrby pilot's actual battery module cost per kilowatt-hour compare with the cost projected in the paper describing its chemistry?
reference_answer: Norrby paid 71 US dollars per kWh for the modules, against the paper's projected 62 US dollars per kWh at cell level.

evidence.quote: The battery modules alone cost 71 US dollars per kilowatt-hour of capacity
we estimate a manufacturing cost of 62 US dollars per kilowatt-hour at the cell level

question: What do the documents report about heat as a risk for room-temperature sodium-sulfur batteries?
reference_answer: The KestrelCell paper finds capacity fade accelerates sharply above 40 degrees Celsius (about 900 cycles at 45 degrees); at Norrby a module overheated at 43 degrees outdoor temperature after a cooling fan failed, and the operators added fan monitoring and reduce charging above 35 degrees.

evidence.quote: capacity fade accelerated sharply above 40 degrees Celsius
a cooling fan in module 17 had failed some days earlier without raising an alarm

question: Compare the KestrelCell with the earlier SodaCore design.
reference_answer: KestrelCell reaches about 2,400 cycles to 80 percent capacity versus about 1,100 for SodaCore (2022), by combining a microporous cathode, a low-solubility electrolyte and an alloy-coated anode.

evidence.quote: the SodaCore design, tested under a similar protocol, reached about 1,100 cycles

question: What is the flash point of VX-9, and how many cell test channels does the Oskarsund centre have?
reference_answer: VX-9's flash point is 112 degrees Celsius; Oskarsund has 512 cell test channels (plus 24 module channels).

evidence.quote: The flash point of VX-9 is 112 degrees Celsius
The centre has 512 test channels for cells up to 20 ampere-hours

question: Summarize this document.
reference_answer: An independent, EN 6240-accredited battery test centre directed by Dr. Amara Lindqvist, with 512 cell and 24 module channels; standard cycle-life tests at 25 degrees and accelerated ageing at 45 degrees; raw data kept 10 years; fees per channel per week with an academic discount.

question: What calendar life, in years, did the KestrelCell paper report?
reference_answer: The paper did not measure or report calendar ageing; it explicitly makes no claims about it. (Registry calendar-life figures belong to other cells.)

evidence.quote: We have not measured calendar ageing

question: How many cycles did the Norrby pilot's cells reach in testing at the Drammen Battery Lab?
reference_answer: The documents don't say: Drammen tested the LFP pilots' cells; the Norrby chemistry was cycle-tested at Oskarsund, and the Norrby report gives no Drammen results.
